etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle English ternysshen, from Old French terniss-, stem of ternir (“to make dim, make wan”), borrowed from Old High German *ternen, tarnen, from Proto-West Germanic *darnijan (“to conceal”). Doublet of dern and darn.
senses: Oxidation or discoloration, especially of a decorative metal exposed to air.
(intransitive) To oxidize or discolor due to oxidation.
(transitive) To compromise, damage, soil, or sully.
